en: The Triplet on the Visible (Sanidassanattika) and the Triplet on Internal Objects (Ajjhattārammaṇattika).

Dependent on a state that is non-demonstrable, non-reacting, and internal as its object, there arises a state that is not non-demonstrable, not non-reacting, and not internal as its object, by way of root condition (*hetu-paccaya*) … [In the case of root:
six; [in the case of predominance: six … [and so on] … [in the case of mutuality: three … [and so on] … [in the case of non-disappearance: six.

Dependent on a state that is non-demonstrable, non-reacting, and external as its object, there arises a state that is not non-demonstrable, not non-reacting, and not external as its object … [and so on].

A state arises by way of root-condition. Dependent on a state that is non-demonstrable, non-reacting, and external as its object, there arises a state that is not non-demonstrable and reacting, and not not-external as its object, by way of root-condition.

Dependent on a state that is non-demonstrable, non-reacting, and external as its object, there arises a state that is not non-demonstrable and reacting, and not not-external as its object... [by way of root-condition].

Arisen by way of root-condition …pe… dependent on a state that is non-demonstrable, non-reacting, and external as object, there arise states that are neither demonstrable nor reacting, nor external as object, and neither non-demonstrable nor reacting, nor external as object, by way of root-condition.
(Abbreviated. There are six [conditions] for root; six for predominance …pe… for mutuality.
Three ... [and so on] ... six non-disappearances. (The Chapter of Questions should be expanded in detail.)
